newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia MinFins up in nervous trade,await U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Russia MinFins up in nervous trade,await U.S. data.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds edged up following the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond rise amid nervousness before U.S. economic data, dealers said on Tuesday.

They said the market, which is near a peak, could react strongly to the figures. From Wednesday to Friday, the U.S. will issue a slew of economic indicators, including the crucial umemployment figure at the end of the week.
"The market opened higher following the rise in the (U.S.) long bond," a Russian dealer said.

"There is a lot of nervousness, and the market is heavy. Some people are trying to cut their risky positions ahead of the U.S. figures. Others are betting the figures will be bullish for the bonds," the dealer said.
On Tuesday, the U.S. said its second-quarter Employment Cost Index rose by 0.8 percent after a 0.6 percent advance in the first quarter.
The market took Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments last week to mean the Fed would watch the index closely when determining its monetary policy, dealers said.
Although the index rose more than the market expected, it was still in a near-two year range and did not affect the MinFin bond market, a Western dealer said.
He said the market was poised for range-bound, nervous trading in the next few days.
"People will be looking for an excuse to either sell everything or buy everything," he said.
"Now, everything is very high, so it can fall or rise sharply depending on the figures. The market is in for extremes, either up or down."
